question: What is the minimum and maximum length of an Erasmus+ study period abroad?
reference_answer: From 2 months (or one academic term or trimester) to 12 months of physical mobility, excluding travel time.

question: ¿Cuántos meses de Erasmus puedo hacer en total durante el grado?
reference_answer: Up to 12 months of physical mobility in total per study cycle (bachelor), regardless of the number and type of mobility periods.

question: I study medicine, which is a one-cycle programme. How long can I be mobile with Erasmus+?
reference_answer: In one-cycle study programmes such as medicine, students can be mobile for up to 24 months.

question: Can recent graduates do an Erasmus+ traineeship, and by when must they finish it?
reference_answer: Yes. They must be selected by their university during their last year of study and complete the traineeship abroad within one year of graduating.

question: Can I do a short stay abroad instead of a full semester? How long must the stay be?
reference_answer: Yes, as a blended short-term mobility: 5 to 30 days of physical mobility (excluding travel time) combined with a compulsory virtual component.

question: What is the minimum number of ECTS credits a blended mobility for studies must award?
reference_answer: A blended mobility for studies must award a minimum of 3 ECTS credits.

question: Does my Erasmus+ study period have to be part of my degree?
reference_answer: Yes. The study period abroad must be part of the student's study programme to complete a degree.

question: ¿En qué grupo de países está España para la beca Erasmus?
reference_answer: Spain is in Group 2, countries with medium living costs.

question: What is the monthly range of the medium range EU Erasmus+ grant?
reference_answer: Between 292 and 606 EUR per month, for mobility to a country with similar living costs.

question: How much is the monthly top-up for students with fewer opportunities on long-term mobility?
reference_answer: 250 EUR per month on top of the individual support; the criteria are defined at national level.

question: How much extra per month do students on an Erasmus+ traineeship receive?
reference_answer: A top-up of 150 EUR per month.

question: How much individual support do I get per day on a short-term physical mobility?
reference_answer: 79 EUR per day up to the 14th day, and 56 EUR per day from the 15th to the 30th day.

question: What counts as green travel in Erasmus+?
reference_answer: Travel using low-emission means of transport (bus, train, bike, car-pooling) for at least half of the round trip; a boat counts if combined with low-emission transport.

question: How many travel days can be covered by individual support if I travel with low-emission transport?
reference_answer: Up to six travel days with low-emission transport, compared with a maximum of two travel days otherwise.

question: Can I go on Erasmus+ without receiving an Erasmus+ grant?
reference_answer: Yes, as a zero-grant participant who meets all criteria and has the same advantages; other grants can be received instead. Participants with fewer opportunities cannot be zero-grant.

question: ¿Tengo que pagar matrícula en la universidad de destino?
reference_answer: No. The host university cannot charge fees for tuition, registration, examinations or access to laboratories and libraries. Small fees (e.g. insurance, student unions) may be charged on the same basis as to local students.

question: Who has to approve the learning agreement, and when?
reference_answer: All parties (the student, the sending and the receiving institution) must digitally approve the learning agreement before the start of the mobility.

question: ¿Puedo cambiar las asignaturas de mi learning agreement cuando ya estoy en el destino?
expected_location: Exceptional changes to the study programme
reference_answer: Only exceptionally. The student can initiate changes within five weeks after the start of each semester, and all parties should agree within two weeks of the request.

question: When must the host university send my transcript of records?
expected_location: Transcript of Records at the receiving institution
reference_answer: Within the period set in the inter-institutional agreement, normally within five weeks after the student's results are published.

question: If only my credits are transferred and not my grades, does it still count as automatic recognition?
expected_location: Does it count as full automatic recognition if...?
reference_answer: Yes, as long as the credits were approved in the learning agreement, confirmed in the transcript of records, and no additional work is required.

question: How many ECTS credits is a normal full academic year?
reference_answer: 60 ECTS credits; for shorter periods the learning agreement is adjusted proportionally.

question: What goes in Table A and Table B of the learning agreement?
reference_answer: Table A lists the components taken at the receiving institution; Table B lists the components they replace at the sending institution. No one-to-one match is needed, but the total credits should correspond.

question: When will the first Erasmus grant payment reach my bank account?
expected_location: Before the mobility period > Your entitlements
reference_answer: A pre-financing payment within 30 calendar days after both parties sign the grant agreement (or after confirmation of arrival), and no later than the start of the mobility period; the exact date depends on the home university.

question: Estudio en España y me voy a Alemania. ¿Qué tramo de beca me corresponde y de cuánto es?
reference_answer: Spain is Group 2 and Germany Group 1, so the higher range EU grant applies: between 348 and 674 EUR per month (the medium range plus at least 50 EUR).

question: I'm a Spanish student going to Poland for a semester and I have fewer opportunities. How much do I get per month?
reference_answer: Group 2 to Group 3 gives the lower range EU grant (225 to 550 EUR per month), plus the fewer-opportunities top-up of 250 EUR per month.

question: I did 5 months of Erasmus during my bachelor. Can I do a 9-month traineeship after graduating?
reference_answer: No. A recent graduate traineeship counts towards the 12-month maximum of the bachelor cycle, so only 7 months are left.

question: I want to do a 3-week blended programme abroad. What are the rules and how much would I get?
reference_answer: It is allowed: 5 to 30 days of physical mobility combined with a compulsory virtual component. For 21 days: 14 x 79 + 7 x 56 = 1,498 EUR.

question: If I change courses during my stay, are the new courses still recognised automatically?
expected_location: Exceptional changes to the study programme;Does it count as full automatic recognition if...?
reference_answer: Yes, if the change was requested within five weeks of the semester start, agreed by all parties, and the latest version of the learning agreement is signed by all parties.

question: I have fewer opportunities and want to do a traineeship abroad. Which top-ups can I receive?
reference_answer: Both: the fewer-opportunities top-up (250 EUR per month) and the traineeship top-up (150 EUR per month).

question: Before I leave, what information am I entitled to and what do I have to sign?
expected_location: Before the mobility period > Your entitlements;Signing the learning agreement
reference_answer: Information on recognition and grading, insurance, housing and visas; and the learning agreement, which all parties must approve digitally before the mobility starts.

question: What exact monthly amount does SEPIE pay Spanish students going to Italy in 2026/27?
reference_answer: The documents only give the EU minimum and maximum ranges; the exact amounts are set by the National Agency or the university and published on their websites. Ask SEPIE or your home university.

question: When is the Erasmus application deadline at my university?
reference_answer: The documents do not contain student application deadlines; each university sets its own. Ask your international office. (The 19 February deadline in the Programme Guide is for universities applying for funding, not for students.)

question: What GPA or language certificate do I need to be selected for Erasmus?
reference_answer: The documents do not cover student selection criteria; they are set by the home university.

question: Do I have to pay tax on my Erasmus grant in Spain?
reference_answer: The documents do not cover taxation of the grant.

question: How many Erasmus places does my university have at the University of Bologna?
reference_answer: The documents do not cover places at specific universities; each university publishes its own offer.

question: Can my Erasmus grant be paid into a bank account outside Spain, for example a German one?
reference_answer: The documents do not cover how or into which bank account the grant is paid; ask the home university, which pays the grant under the student's grant agreement.
